question: Can I Offer Net-30 Invoicing as a Payment Method for B2B Customers?
metaDescription: Yes, through a dedicated B2B/wholesale plugin — this isn't a standard gateway, since it defers payment rather than collecting it at checkout.
shortAnswer: Yes, but it's fundamentally different from a normal payment gateway, since the whole point is deferring collection rather than charging immediately at checkout. A dedicated B2B/wholesale plugin is the practical way to implement this — typically restricting the option to approved accounts, generating a formal invoice with defined terms, and tracking payment status separately from the usual instant-gateway order flow.

bodyHtml:
Why This Needs a Dedicated Approach

A standard payment gateway is built around collecting money at (or very near) the point of order, which is the opposite of what net-30 terms require. B2B and wholesale plugins for WooCommerce handle this properly: restricting the payment option to specific approved customer accounts (since not every buyer should be extended credit terms), generating a proper invoice with the agreed due date, and tracking whether it's been paid separately from the order's fulfillment status.

Things to Get Right

  • Account approval and credit limits need a clear process — not every business customer should automatically qualify for net terms, and most B2B plugins support a manual approval step or a defined credit limit per account.
  • Order fulfillment and payment status are separate concerns under net terms — an order might ship well before payment is actually due or received, which needs to be reflected clearly in how the order is tracked internally.
  • Overdue invoice handling (reminders, late fees, account holds for repeat late payers) is worth planning for explicitly rather than leaving it purely manual and easy to overlook.
  • Accounting integration matters more here than with instant-gateway payments, since net terms genuinely change how revenue and receivables need to be tracked.

Setting This Up

  1. Choose a B2B/wholesale plugin built specifically for approved-account, net-terms invoicing, rather than trying to adapt a standard gateway for this purpose.
  2. Define the account approval and credit-limit process clearly before launching the option to any customers.
  3. Set up a clear overdue-invoice workflow, including reminders and any late-fee or account-hold policy.
